items.title: Flip, Don't Shuffle: Watermarking LLMs at the Speed of Inference
items.one_liner: SBW provides a near-zero-overhead LLM watermarking mechanism suitable for high-throughput distributed inference pipelines.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced Stateless Bernoulli Watermarking (SBW), an O(1) statistical watermarking method for Large Language Models that determines green list membership via independent per-token Bernoulli trials. Unlike existing approaches like KGW or SynthID, SBW requires only a single comparison against a counter-based random number generator, enabling single-kernel GPU execution with zero intermediate allocations. The technique supports full-vocabulary self-salt watermarking at over 6,000 times the speed of KGW and adds less than 1% overhead across batch sizes in generation benchmarks. Detection guarantees remain equivalent to fixed-size green list methods while preserving text diversity.
key_facts: Performance: Under 1% overhead across batch sizes
items.bottom_line: Stateless Bernoulli Watermarking eliminates the computational bottleneck of LLM watermarking by enabling single-kernel O(1) execution with under 1% latency overhead.
